title: Lua: Treat plugin directories with `init.lua` as package
description:
This changes the loading logic of lua plugins such that any directory in the global or personal plugin directories that contains a `init.lua` are treated as packages to be loaded as `require "dirname"`. The init.lua script is the entry point and responsible for loading any additional submodules that may exist in the tree

AI-Assisted: no

Test case:

[plugins.tar.gz](/uploads/c43c87fa3a5349c2669e7f9a37536f6e/plugins.tar.gz)

The archive expands into a plugins directory:

* plugins/init.lua - the root init.lua, should always be loaded
* plugins/a_package
  * only file loaded directly by wireshark should be init.lua, it will require the rest (except assert.lua)
* plugins/not_a_package/
  * loaded recursively by wireshark

notes.body: I think this makes sense, but I don't have time to test it at the moment. It would be nice if someone else who uses Lua a lot could test this.

https://wiki.wireshark.org/lua#how-lua-fits-into-wireshark  
  
`init.lua` has special meaning - includes startup variables.  
Should the filename be different when its used with package folders?

That’s a fair question, given the special meaning of `init.lua` in the configuration directory.

In standard Lua, `init.lua` is the conventional entry point for a package directory (via the default `require` search path). The intent here is not to change the meaning of the existing top-level `init.lua`, but to apply the conventional Lua package semantics to subdirectories in the plugin folders.

So the idea would be: keep the current special handling for the root `init.lua` for backwards compatibility, while allowing `*/init.lua` to behave as a package entry in nested plugin directories. This aligns with how other Lua hosts scope their own startup `init.lua` versus library modules, and avoids introducing a Wireshark-specific naming convention for packages.
